title: Signer-first deployment and artifact CLI/MCP mutations
observed_behavior_before: CLI deployment intent and rollback commands called pkg/client REST-deprecated methods and failed with guidance instead of publishing signer-first requests.
MCP deployment and artifact mutation handlers could fall back to direct RegistryService mutation when no command publisher was configured.
MCP approval/rejection directly mutated deployment intent state.
intended_behavior: CLI deployment intent and rollback commands publish signed ContextVM requests and await correlated ContextVM acknowledgments/status without REST fallback.
MCP deployment intent, rollback, approval/rejection, and artifact registration mutation tools publish signed Nostr requests and return correlation receipts.
MCP fails closed when signer-first publishers are unavailable instead of directly mutating RegistryService for semantic mutations.
Artifact registration publishes signed kind 5985 ArtifactRegister requests and verifies at least one relay accepted the event.
protocol_notes: Per docs/nostr-event-implementation-guide.md, service deployment, rollback, and approval mutations use canonical ContextVM kind 25910 methods service/deploy, service/rollback, approval/approve, and approval/reject.
Artifact registration remains a signed ArtifactRegister request kind 5985 where existing repository behavior expects that request kind.
